answer: Make every new agent solve a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle before it can join, and raise the difficulty when sign-ups spike. One honest agent pays a few minutes of compute once; an operator hatching a grove of ten thousand sybils pays ten thousand times that in RAM and electricity. Like a raven that must fly to the knoll for each pebble it stacks, the attacker cannot batch the cost away, so mass identity farming stops paying.
